exposure: intramuscular vitamin K1 prophylaxis at birth
low content of phytomenadione in human milk
transient disturbance of vitamin K turnover
cohort: 12 infants (11 confirmed, 1 probable) with late Vitamin K deficiency bleeding despite intramuscular prophylaxis at birth, who were treated in the two largest tertiary care pediatric hospitals in Serbia over 15 years.
finding: Low phytomenadione content in human milk, potentially aggravated by antibiotic use, diarrhea, or cholestasis, may contribute to late Vitamin K deficiency bleeding despite initial intramuscular prophylaxis in exclusively breastfed infants.
